page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor architecture operating at 2.8 GHz. The system features 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation tasks all ranking in the top tier. Memory performance is a key strength, with DDR5 memory bandwidth and Passmark memory scores placing in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores landing in the average tier.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression, achieving top-tier results in Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests. While medium and large LLM text generation speeds are strong, small-model text generation is poor, indicating that the architecture is better suited for larger parallel workloads rather than low-latency single-threaded tasks. This bare-metal instance is highly efficient for high-density container orchestration, large-scale web serving, software compilation, and database hosting.
description: The Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server featuring 96 dedicated physical cores on the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory, it provides a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The server delivers top-tier multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations, as evidenced by outstanding results in multi-threaded benchmarks, Redis SET operations, and software compilation. Conversely, single-core performance remains average, and text generation for small language models is a notable bottleneck. With a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, this instance is highly suited for parallelized workloads, including database hosting, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation, offering strong resource density and qualitative cost-efficiency for multi-threaded enterprise applications.
